title: Normal Noetherian approximation of a pointed smooth family
statement:
Let $S$ be a quasi-compact quasi-separated integral scheme with integrally closed stalks
[def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions, def-sbc-normal-dominant-galois]. Let $c:C\to S$ be
quasi-compact, quasi-separated, smooth [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms], and geometrically connected.
Let $\sigma:S\to C$ satisfy $\sigma c=1_S$, and let $n\in\mathbf N$ be invertible in
$\Gamma(S,\mathcal O_S)$. There exist a small cofiltered category $I$, diagrams
$X,Y:I\to\mathrm{Scheme}$, limiting cones $\alpha:S\to X$ and $\gamma:C\to Y$, and
natural transformations $p:Y\to X$ and $\tau:X\to Y$. Every $X_i$ is integral,
Noetherian, quasi-separated, and has integrally closed stalks. The transition maps of $X$
are affine and every $\alpha_i$ is dominant. Every square $(c,\gamma_i,\alpha_i,p_i)$
is a pullback [def-pc-fibre-product], and for every arrow $f:i\to j$ the square
$(Y(f),p_i,p_j,X(f))$ is a pullback. The equalities
$\sigma\gamma_i=\alpha_i\tau_i$ and $\tau_i p_i=1_{X_i}$ hold. Every $p_i$ is
quasi-compact, quasi-separated, smooth and geometrically connected, and $n$ is invertible
in $\Gamma(X_i,\mathcal O_{X_i})$.

proof.text: Apply absolute Noetherian approximation to S. Replace every stage by the normalization of its integral scheme-theoretic image in its own fraction field. Finiteness of normalization over the integers gives Noetherian normal integral stages. Normality of S factors its projections through these stages; uniqueness supplies transition maps, and dominance follows from the image construction. The affine chart rings embed in the rings of S, contain the old image rings, and their union is the ring of S, so the new affine transition system still has limit S.

Descend the finitely presented smooth family and its section, including its section equation, to one stage; smoothness descends by Tag 0C0C. Restrict to the open component through the section. On every geometric fibre the original connected fibre meets this component and therefore maps into it; hence its pullback is all of C. This open model is quasi-compact since it is an open of a Noetherian family. Descend the inverse of n on a finite affine cover, and agreement on affine covers of overlaps. Pass to a cofiltered tail and take all later families and sections by base change. Their transition squares and comparison squares are cartesian; base change preserves smoothness and geometric connectedness and preserves the unit n. Base change of the fixed family gives its limit cone and the section compatibility.

theorem exists_normal_pointed_family_approximation {S C : Scheme.{u}} [CompactSpace S]
    [QuasiSeparatedSpace S] [IsIntegral S]
    (hS : ∀ x : S, IsIntegrallyClosed (S.presheaf.stalk x))
    (c : C ⟶ S) [QuasiCompact c] [QuasiSeparated c] [Smooth c] [GeometricallyConnected c]
    (σ : S ⟶ C) (hσ : σ ≫ c = 𝟙 S) (n : ℕ) (hn : IsUnit (n : Γ(S, ⊤))) :
    ∃ (I : Type u) (hcat : SmallCategory I),
      letI : SmallCategory I := hcat
      ∃ (hco : IsCofiltered I) (X Y : I ⥤ Scheme.{u})
        (α : (Functor.const I).obj S ⟶ X) (γ : (Functor.const I).obj C ⟶ Y)
        (hα : IsLimit (Cone.mk S α)) (hγ : IsLimit (Cone.mk C γ))
        (p : Y ⟶ X) (τ : X ⟶ Y) (hI : ∀ i, IsIntegral (X.obj i)),
        (∀ {i j : I} (f : i ⟶ j), IsAffineHom (X.map f)) ∧
        (∀ i, IsDominant (α.app i)) ∧
        (∀ i, IsPullback c (γ.app i) (α.app i) (p.app i)) ∧
        (∀ {i j : I} (f : i ⟶ j),
          IsPullback (Y.map f) (p.app i) (p.app j) (X.map f)) ∧
        (∀ i, σ ≫ γ.app i = α.app i ≫ τ.app i) ∧
        (∀ i, IsNoetherian (X.obj i) ∧ QuasiSeparatedSpace (X.obj i) ∧
          (∀ x : X.obj i, IsIntegrallyClosed ((X.obj i).presheaf.stalk x)) ∧
          QuasiCompact (p.app i) ∧ QuasiSeparated (p.app i) ∧ Smooth (p.app i) ∧
          GeometricallyConnected (p.app i) ∧ τ.app i ≫ p.app i = 𝟙 (X.obj i) ∧
          IsUnit (n : Γ(X.obj i, ⊤)))
